headline: Symbiosis is mutual benefit—species that help each other both do better than either alone
universal_truth: Cooperation can beat competition; mutual benefit relationships create value for all parties
fun_facts: Clownfish live in anemones—the fish gets protection, the anemone gets food scraps and cleaning
Your gut contains trillions of bacteria that help you digest food—you feed them, they help you
Trees in forests share nutrients through underground fungal networks, helping each other survive
discussion_questions: What mutually beneficial relationships do you have?
What relationships drain you versus energize you?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: The clownfish lives among anemone tentacles that would kill other fish. Why doesn't it get stung? They have a deal. The fish brings food and cleans parasites. The anemone provides protection. Both benefit. This is symbiosis.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often assume nature is competition—survival of the fittest. But cooperation is everywhere. What makes mutual benefit work?

options.text: Symbiosis works when each party provides something the other needs at lower cost than they could get it alone—specialization plus exchange creates mutual gain
options.response: Yes. Trade works because different species have different abilities. What's easy for you may be hard for me, and vice versa. Cooperation lets both parties gain.

options.text: Some species just naturally get along
options.response: It's not just compatibility—it's mutual benefit that makes relationships stable...

q1.title: Mutual Benefit
q1.script: True symbiosis benefits both parties. Unlike parasitism where one gains at another's expense, mutualism creates win-win. Both species are better off together than apart.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Mutual Benefit"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Specialization Trade
q2.script: Symbiosis often involves specialization. You're good at X, I'm good at Y. By trading, we both get X and Y without each mastering both. Specialization plus exchange beats self-sufficiency.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Human Symbiosis
q3.script: Your life is full of symbiosis—relationships where both parties benefit. Good partnerships, healthy communities, fair trades. Seek and nurture mutual benefit relationships.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Cooperation can beat competition. Mutual benefit relationships create value for all parties. Seek win-win connections.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 252. Tomorrow, we'll explore living off others—parasitism. Until then, identify a mutually beneficial relationship in your life.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Symbiosis Check - Who Benefits?
growTrack.activity: Map a key relationship: what do you provide? What do you receive? Is it mutual benefit, or is one party gaining at the other's expense? Healthy relationships are symbiotic—both parties better off than alone.
